title: The Man Who Stopped on the Road
idea: The parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:25-37) retold in plain words: a traveller is robbed on the road to Jericho, a priest and a Levite cross to the other side, and a Samaritan stops, cares for him and pays for his stay; Jesus asks the lawyer which one was the neighbour

cast.name: Jesus
cast.look: calm teacher, plain white robe, short brown beard, sandals

cast.name: Lawyer
cast.look: sharp lawyer, long grey robe, a scroll in his hand, thin beard

cast.name: Samaritan
cast.look: practical traveller, brown tunic, a travel bag and a donkey

cast.name: Innkeeper
cast.look: innkeeper, round face, red apron, hair in a scarf

scenes.title: The question
scenes.place: a grassy hillside above the lake, a crowd sitting in the sun and a lawyer standing up

lines.t: A lawyer tested Jesus with a question. He answered with a road.
Crowds followed Jesus everywhere, and this man wanted to catch him out.
A lawyer is a man who knows the rules. He wanted to know exactly where they stopped.
Teacher, the law says to love my neighbour. But who is my neighbour?
He wanted a short list. A line to draw, with some people on each side.
Jesus did not give him a list. He told him a story.
It is a parable Jesus told, and it begins on a very lonely road.

scenes.title: The road
scenes.place: the steep rocky road down from Jerusalem to Jericho, bare hills and a few boulders

lines.t: A man was walking from Jerusalem down to Jericho. It was a long, steep road, and a dangerous one.
The hills hid robbers, and travellers there kept their eyes open and their bags close.
This man walked alone. He was tired, and he was not thinking about danger.
The sun was high and the road was empty, and the heat shimmered on the stones.
Then, in a bend of the road, the robbers stepped out.
When they were gone, the road was quiet. The man lay by the side of it, and his bag was gone.
He could not stand. He could not call out. He could only wait for someone to come.

scenes.title: The other side
scenes.place: the steep rocky road down from Jerusalem to Jericho, bare hills and a few boulders

lines.t: The first to come was a priest. A respected man, with an important place to be.
He saw the man lying there. And he crossed to the other side of the road.
Maybe he was late. Maybe he was afraid. Maybe he told himself someone else would help.
He walked on. His steps got faster, not slower.
Then came a Levite, a man who served in the temple. He came close enough to look.
He looked. And he, too, crossed to the other side.
Two good men, two good reasons, and one man still lying on the road.
The road was empty again, except for the dust, and one man waiting.

scenes.title: The Samaritan
scenes.place: the steep rocky road down from Jerusalem to Jericho, bare hills and a few boulders

lines.t: The third traveller was a Samaritan. The people listening to Jesus looked down on Samaritans.
He had every reason to keep walking. He did not.
He did not ask who the man was. He did not ask where he came from.
He stopped. He knelt in the dust beside the stranger.
The robbers might still be close. He knelt there anyway.
Hold on, friend. You are not alone now.
He cleaned and bandaged him, using the oil and wine he carried for his own journey.
Then he lifted him onto his own donkey, and walked beside him, one slow step at a time.
It cost him time, and it cost him money. He did not count either.

scenes.title: The inn
scenes.place: a small roadside inn at night, a lamp, a bed and a courtyard with a donkey

lines.t: They reached an inn as the sun went down. The Samaritan did not leave him at the door.
He carried the man in, found him a bed, and stayed with him all night.
Is there a room? He needs rest, and food, and someone to watch over him.
All night he stayed by the bed, changing the bandages by lamplight.
There is. But a room costs money, friend. Who is going to pay for it?
The Samaritan nodded. He had already thought of that.

scenes.title: Two coins
scenes.place: the inn courtyard in the morning, the innkeeper's table and the road beyond the gate

lines.t: In the morning, the Samaritan had to go. But he did not just walk away.
He took out two silver coins, and put them in the innkeeper's hand.
Look after him. If it costs more, I will pay you when I come back.
He did not ask the man his name. He did not ask what he believed.
Then he went on his way, and the innkeeper looked after the stranger.
He saw a man who needed help, and he was the one standing there.

scenes.title: Which one
scenes.place: a grassy hillside above the lake, a crowd sitting in the sun and a lawyer standing up

lines.t: Jesus looked at the lawyer, and asked him one question.
Which of these three was a neighbour to the man the robbers left on the road?
The one who showed him mercy.
Go, and do the same.
The lawyer said nothing for a long moment. Everyone listening knew who had stopped.
The lawyer had asked who counts as a neighbour. Jesus turned the question around.
Not, who deserves my help? But, will I be the one who stops?
Jesus did not tell him who to help. He told him who to become.
Everyone has a road like that. And everyone has someone lying beside it.
Who is on the other side of your road this week?
